key_insight: For geometry-aware hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and finite-element physical consistency are more effective during fine-tuning than early or continuous training.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate synthetic aortic CFD solutions with automatically adjusted physiological boundary conditions.
Represent anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and train Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net surrogates.
Investigate active learning and differentiable finite-element residual constraints to improve data efficiency and accuracy.
evidence_signal: Peak-systolic evaluations show fine-tuning benefits from gradient- and subspace-based acquisition and physical consistency constraints, while out-of-distribution tests identify geometric coverage as the main limitation.
watch_item: Generalization remains limited by the geometric support of the anatomy parametrization; architectural changes alone may not address unseen shapes.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
